cases.description: Non-positive weight raises ValueError before any fee branch runs.
cases.input_strategy: Parametrize weight in {0, -1, -0.5} — all satisfy weight <= 0; any param representative of the same exception path. Separate the exact zero boundary and negative case in one parametrized set since both hit the same raise; keep distinct from normal weights.
cases.expected_behavior: ValueError('weight must be positive') is raised for every weight <= 0, including default express=False and express=True.

cases.description: Upper bound of first tier at weight exactly 1 inclusive, and just above 1 drops to tier 2 — opposite sides of the <=1 threshold.
cases.input_strategy: Two representative inputs: weight=1 (inclusive tier edge) and weight=1+epsilon (e.g. 1.0001) crossing the threshold.

cases.description: Upper bound of second tier at weight exactly 5 inclusive, and just above 5 drops to tier 3 — opposite sides of the <=5 threshold.
cases.input_strategy: Two representative inputs: weight=5 (inclusive tier edge) and weight=5+epsilon (e.g. 5.0001) crossing the threshold.

cases.description: Interior representative weight in each tier returns the expected base fee.
cases.input_strategy: Parametrize one interior point per tier: e.g. (0.5 -> 5), (2 -> 10), (10 -> 20). Interior values, not the boundary cases above.
cases.expected_behavior: Fee is 5, 10, 20 respectively for the three interior weights with express=False.

cases.description: Express flag adds flat 8 to the tier fee across all tiers.
cases.input_strategy: Parametrize (weight, expected_express_fee) covering one weight per tier: (0.5 -> 13), (2 -> 18), (10 -> 28). Use interior values distinct from boundary cases to avoid duplicating them.
cases.expected_behavior: Express result equals tier fee + 8 for each tier.

cases.description: Classification is by weight tier, not express; express must not shift a weight into another tier. Verify express boundary behavior at exactly 1 and 5.
cases.input_strategy: Parametrize (weight=1 -> 13), (weight=5 -> 18) with express=True to confirm tier boundaries are identical with and without express.
cases.expected_behavior: shipping_fee(1, express=True) == 13 and shipping_fee(5, express=True) == 18, proving express only adds 8 without altering tier selection.

cases.description: Default express argument is False so fee equals base tier amount with two-arg-style one-arg call.
cases.input_strategy: Call shipping_fee(2) using only the weight argument; assert equals 10.
cases.expected_behavior: Omitting express yields base fee 10, same as express=False.

payload.diagnosis: All 19 collected test cases passed with zero failures, errors, or skips (execution.json: returncode 0, 19 passed). Coverage is 100% line and 100% branch on shipping.py, well above the 80% line / 70% branch thresholds, with no missing lines or branches. The test suite independently exercises the raise-nonpositive exception path (both express values), both upper-tier boundaries (1 and 5 inclusive plus epsilon above each), interior representatives of all three tiers, express flat surcharge across tiers, express-preserves-tier at boundaries, and the default-express=False behavior — matching the source contract in shipping_fee. Independent quality observation: epsilon values (1.0001, 5.0001) are reasonable stand-ins for 'just above' but are not guaranteed minimal crossings for all float representations; a strict reviewer might prefer math.nextafter for exact threshold adjacency. This is a minor robustness suggestion only and does not affect the current green result. No evidence of test generation errors, source contract inconsistencies, or environment issues.
payload.uncertainty: None material. The only residual concern is that boundary-adjacent values use fixed epsilon literals rather than exact next-representable floats; this does not weaken the passing verdict because actual source comparisons use <= on the same literals tested.
